sources.title: AI UX Playground
sources.author: AI UX Playground
sources.shows: Named patterns for citations, control, streaming, memory and agent actions.
sources.application: Useful foundation for evidence cards, readable conversation and bounded agency.
sources.limits: Selected relevant entries reviewed; the entire catalogue was not audited. Its FAQ currently describes 150 patterns in 11 categories.

sources.title: AI Interaction Atlas
sources.author: Brandon Harwood · quietloudlab
sources.shows: Separates human tasks, AI tasks, system tasks, data artifacts, constraints and touchpoints.
sources.application: Use its vocabulary to assign review, execution, state management and recovery responsibilities.
sources.limits: A taxonomy, not a prescriptive UI framework. The official repository is available at https://github.com/quietloudlab/ai-interaction-atlas under Apache 2.0.

sources.title: GenAI UX Design Patterns
sources.author: Sharang Sharma
sources.shows: Organises design around needs, trust, control, errors and safety.
sources.application: Use these lenses to assess a family of patterns rather than treating AI as a single chat feature.
sources.limits: The public overview supports this synthesis; linked material and individual examples were not exhaustively audited.

sources.title: The Shape of AI
sources.author: Emily Campbell
sources.shows: Connects wayfinding, contextual inputs, human oversight and trust cues.
sources.application: Adapt citations, memory control, disclosure and contextual actions to Scripture and personal practice.
sources.limits: The site states CC BY NC SA. This reference uses original text and original wireframes; it does not reproduce the source illustrations.

sources.title: 8 voice AI UX patterns
sources.author: Sharang Sharma
sources.shows: Compares voice modes including turn-taking, voice-augmented chat, dictation and ambient access.
sources.application: Separate narrated audio from capture and dialogue; make roles and interruption clear.
sources.limits: A design analysis rather than a clinical or Bible-app validation study. The original short link leads through another Friedman post.

sources.title: Agentic UX Patterns
sources.author: Dustin Kirk
sources.shows: Highlights role contracts, delegation modes, human oversight, grounding, memory and repair.
sources.application: Inform capability boundaries, source-bounded explanation and action recovery.
sources.limits: The catalogue presents 49 proposals. Their inclusion is not evidence of effectiveness in faith or clinical settings.

sources.title: Design Patterns Catalogue
sources.author: Projects by IF
sources.shows: Offers interaction approaches for data use, trust, accountability and control.
sources.application: Inform private sharing, purpose-specific choices and manageable automation.
sources.limits: Broader than AI; data-control interfaces must be backed by corresponding storage and permission behaviour.

sources.title: Voice of AI
sources.author: Anne Cantera
sources.shows: Covers conversation, persona, context, memory, multimodality, evaluation and guardrails.
sources.application: A curriculum map for voice-state design and evaluation questions.
sources.limits: Not every linked learning module was read. The overview does not validate a specific conversation script.

sources.title: Designing Audio AI People Actually Trust
sources.author: Harsheen Vohra
sources.shows: Discusses transparency, voice consent, context, content control, customisation and accessibility.
sources.application: Inform narration provenance and explicit listening versus capture states.
sources.limits: The author scopes this to responsible audio AI, not a complete conversational-agent guideline.

sources.title: Aiverse Design Patterns
sources.author: Kshitij Agrawal, Dave Brown and Clair Sun · credit listed by Vitaly Friedman
sources.shows: Uses product examples across discovery, instruction, observation, refinement and adaptation.
sources.application: Inform the progression from task choice to scope refinement and review; use public examples as further comparison material.
sources.limits: Protected Pro content was not reviewed. Public presentation is not an independent usability study.

sources.title: AI UX Patterns
sources.author: Luke Bennis
sources.shows: Combines help, suggestions, input feedback and result actions in one experience.
sources.application: Inform task entry, editing and review of AI suggestions.
sources.limits: The pattern-composition example is a design reference, not a validation of the proposed faith-specific variants.

sources.title: Pattern Catalogue
sources.author: Maggie Appleton
sources.shows: Includes Historical Trails, Daily Notes and Epistemic Disclosure.
sources.application: Inform reading trails, personal-note entry and explicit evidence status.
sources.limits: A broad observational design catalogue rather than an exclusively AI or faith resource.

sources.title: Where should AI sit in your UI
sources.author: Sharang Sharma
sources.shows: Compares seven spatial arrangements, including inline help, panels and full conversation surfaces.
sources.application: Inform task-centred AI placement and comparisons outside chat bubbles.
sources.limits: Its role interpretations should be tested with the intended audience; they do not establish universal layout rules.

sources.title: How can AI UI capture intent
sources.author: Sharang Sharma
sources.shows: Explores contextual controls for search, uploaded material and content creation.
sources.application: Adapt editable passage context, source scope and concrete task choices.
sources.limits: Avoid turning contextual assistance into hidden inference about belief, health or emotional state.

sources.title: Design Patterns for AI Interfaces
sources.author: Vitaly Friedman
sources.shows: The syllabus covers context, memory, layout, input, output, accessibility, orchestration and evaluation.
sources.application: Use it as a coverage check for missing-context, overflow and governance scenarios.
sources.limits: The course videos were not reviewed. Syllabus content is not treated as tested guidance.

sources.title: 50 AI Design Patterns That Actually Work
sources.author: Vitaly Friedman
sources.shows: Provides a structured teaching format for AI interface decisions and examples.
sources.application: Editorial method: explain a concrete problem, compare alternatives and discuss failure cases.
sources.limits: No course attendance or protected teaching material reviewed; no individual pattern claim is attributed to the course.

sources.title: AI and Design Systems
sources.author: Brad Frost, Ian Frost and TJ Pitre
sources.shows: Connects AI use with reusable components, product development and organisational practice.
sources.application: Implementation lens: the same state, provenance and permission semantics should survive across components.
sources.limits: Paid lessons and community discussions were not reviewed. Course claims are not research evidence.

sources.title: The AI Design Guide
sources.author: Romina Kavcic
sources.shows: Presents agentic design workflows, guides, templates and tools.
sources.application: Workflow lens for reusable briefs and maintaining an atlas alongside a design system.
sources.limits: Protected materials were not reviewed; check the publisher for current course availability.

sources.title: Into Design Systems
sources.author: Sil Bormüller and team · credit listed by Vitaly Friedman
sources.shows: A conference and recording resource for AI and design-system practice.
sources.application: Further-learning and expert-review discovery, rather than a primary basis for an individual interaction rule.
sources.limits: Talks and recordings were not watched. Event marketing does not support a clinical, legal or usability conclusion.

sources.title: Citations
sources.author: AI UX Playground
sources.shows: Connects claims to inspectable sources.
sources.application: Precise verse, document and media evidence.
sources.limits: Citation presence alone does not establish claim support.

sources.title: Progressive Disclosure
sources.author: AI UX Playground
sources.shows: Offers layers of information instead of simultaneous detail.
sources.application: Answer depth and passage preview.
sources.limits: The proposed reader transition is a domain adaptation.

sources.title: Memory Scope Toggle
sources.author: AI UX Playground
sources.shows: Gives memory persistence an explicit scope.
sources.application: Reviewable optional memory with clear purpose.
sources.limits: A faith app still needs data governance and lawful processing.

sources.title: Suggest Confirm Execute
sources.author: AI UX Playground
sources.shows: Separates suggestions, approved changes and execution.
sources.application: Action previews and bounded authority.
sources.limits: Approval thresholds depend on consequence and previously granted permissions.

sources.title: Interrupt and Resume
sources.author: AI UX Playground
sources.shows: Makes interruption and continuation visible.
sources.application: Partial output and recoverable long-answer reading.
sources.limits: Backend recovery must match the UI promise.

sources.title: Control the level of automation
sources.author: Projects by IF
sources.shows: Lets people select an appropriate level of automation.
sources.application: Permissions by capability and consequence.
sources.limits: Standing authority must be bounded and revocable.

sources.title: Scripture structure documentation
sources.author: USFM documentation
sources.shows: Preserves distinctions in Scripture, paragraphs, notes and editorial content.
sources.application: Derive user scenarios from content meaning, not marker names.
sources.limits: A format is not a complete model of app behaviour, annotations or formation.

sources.title: Footnote structure
sources.author: USFM documentation
sources.shows: Documents note caller, origin, quotation and explanatory parts.
sources.application: Keep note parts and anchors intact.
sources.limits: Does not prescribe inline, sheet or panel presentation.

sources.title: Cross-reference structure
sources.author: USFM documentation
sources.shows: Documents cross-reference origins, targets and groups.
sources.application: Preview, compare and return while preserving grouping.
sources.limits: Reference relation does not imply theological agreement.

sources.title: Translation additions
sources.author: USFM documentation
sources.shows: Describes translator-supplied wording that clarifies meaning.
sources.application: Explain the edition convention.
sources.limits: Translation additions are not AI additions.

sources.title: Poetic paragraphs
sources.author: USFM documentation
sources.shows: Describes poetic paragraphs and relative indentation.
sources.application: Preserve poetic relationships through reflow.
sources.limits: Accessible presentation needs testing beyond import correctness.

sources.title: Extended study footnotes
sources.author: USFM documentation
sources.shows: Describes extended study content attached to the text.
sources.application: Publisher note with clear provenance.
sources.limits: A study note is distinct from a personal annotation.

sources.title: Study sidebars
sources.author: USFM documentation
sources.shows: Describes a bounded editorial sidebar.
sources.application: Separate longer excursions from verse text.
sources.limits: Sidebar content remains subject to edition rights.

sources.title: Internal editorial remarks
sources.author: USFM documentation
sources.shows: Describes remarks not intended for publication.
sources.application: Keep internal records out of reader-facing commentary.
sources.limits: Requires import and publishing controls, not only styling.

sources.title: Accessible modal dialog pattern
sources.author: W3C WAI
sources.shows: Specifies modal focus and keyboard behaviour.
sources.application: Accessible note sheets and modal interactions on the web.
sources.limits: Native apps require corresponding platform mechanisms.

sources.title: Understanding Reflow
sources.author: W3C WAI
sources.shows: Explains usable content reflow at constrained width and enlargement.
sources.application: Readable cards, references and comparison layouts.
sources.limits: Some content has defined exceptions; test the actual experience.

sources.title: AI Chatbots Design Guidelines
sources.author: Nielsen Norman Group
sources.shows: Discusses concise output, expanded detail and streaming-scroll problems.
sources.application: Long answers, deliberate expansion and reader-controlled scrolling.
sources.limits: General chatbot research, not validation of these Bible-app patterns.

sources.title: Android Audio Bible
sources.author: YouVersion
sources.shows: Documents playback, navigation, speed, timer and edition availability.
sources.application: Audio-first controls and accurate availability states.
sources.limits: Documented behaviour; no direct product usability audit performed.

sources.title: Dwell Read Along
sources.author: Dwell
sources.shows: Describes combined listening and reading.
sources.application: Continuous read-along as an interaction reference.
sources.limits: Publisher claims about comprehension are not independent study results.

sources.title: Return to the playing verse
sources.author: Dwell
sources.shows: Describes returning from browsing to the verse currently playing.
sources.application: Separate viewport and playback positions.
sources.limits: Behaviour reference, not a fresh hands-on audit.

sources.title: Guided Scripture
sources.author: YouVersion
sources.shows: Documents a guided sequence with media and Scripture.
sources.application: Named stages, navigation and optional media.
sources.limits: The proposed wireframe is an original generalisation.

sources.title: How to pray Lectio Divina
sources.author: Hallow
sources.shows: Explains reading, meditation, prayer and contemplation in this practice.
sources.application: Named phases and intentional silence.
sources.limits: A tradition-specific practice guide, not a universal or clinical protocol.

sources.title: EPUB Media Overlays
sources.author: W3C
sources.shows: Provides a model for synchronised text and audio.
sources.application: Honest timing granularity and playback anchors.
sources.limits: Verify support in the app and edition you intend to use.

sources.title: Record your insights using Notes
sources.author: Logos
sources.shows: Explains notes and selection or reference anchoring.
sources.application: Annotation scope, library and edition changes.
sources.limits: Documentation does not validate all proposed sync or overlap behaviour.

sources.title: Resource Guide
sources.author: Olive Tree
sources.shows: Describes context-related study resources.
sources.application: Contextual previews and linked study panels.
sources.limits: A product reference; its native interface was not independently tested.

sources.title: Evidence-bounded study method
sources.author: Bible & Faith Patterns
sources.shows: Separate evidence, interpretation and missing data.
sources.application: Apply provenance and uncertainty to lexical study.
sources.limits: Not an external empirical source.

sources.title: Digital Spiritual Formation research agenda
sources.author: Bible & Faith Patterns
sources.shows: Defines questions about actual reading, motivation, autonomy and formation.
sources.application: Proposed habit, progress and community patterns.
sources.limits: Further studies require complete citations, methodological review and explicit limitations before their findings inform a pattern.

sources.title: Wysa FAQ
sources.author: Wysa
sources.shows: Describes curated exercises, role boundaries and different rule-based or generative offerings.
sources.application: Reference for controlled content and explicit service scope.
sources.limits: Marketing and provider documentation, not independent efficacy evidence. Wysa is not a crisis service.

sources.title: Woebot FAQ
sources.author: Woebot Health
sources.shows: Records retirement of the app on 30 June 2025.
sources.application: Historical reference for curated conversational content.
sources.limits: Not a currently available app recommendation.

sources.title: Therabot trial overview
sources.author: Dartmouth · 27 March 2025
sources.shows: Reports a randomised study with 106 participants given Therabot and 104 controls without it, with symptom improvements and clinical oversight.
sources.application: Shows why system-specific evidence and oversight matter for health claims.
sources.limits: Not a head-to-head comparison with therapy. Full NEJM AI text was unavailable in this review. Findings do not transfer automatically to general or faith chatbots.

sources.title: Randomized Trial of a Generative AI Chatbot for Mental Health Treatment
sources.author: Heinz and colleagues · NEJM AI · 2025
sources.shows: Original publication associated with the Dartmouth trial.
sources.application: Further review is needed before citing detailed methods or numerical effect estimates from the paper.
sources.limits: Access failure is explicitly recorded; the institutional summary supports the limited account above.

sources.title: Expressing stigma and inappropriate responses prevents LLMs from safely replacing mental health providers
sources.author: Moore and colleagues · FAccT 2025
sources.shows: Experiments found stigma and inappropriate responses, including unsafe handling of delusional beliefs, in tested models.
sources.application: Inform adversarial and multi-turn evaluation for distress and dangerous claims.
sources.limits: Specific models and experimental scenarios; not a measurement of all present or future systems.

sources.title: Concept of Trauma and Guidance for a Trauma-Informed Approach
sources.author: SAMHSA · 2014
sources.shows: Principles include safety, transparency, collaboration, empowerment and cultural sensitivity.
sources.application: Design lens for predictable transitions, voluntary disclosure and accountable data practices.
sources.limits: An organisational approach, not a validated AI script. The full guide needs deeper review before claiming implementation fidelity.

sources.title: Psychological first aid Guide for field workers
sources.author: WHO, War Trauma Foundation and World Vision International · 2011
sources.shows: Frames humane practical support with respect for dignity, culture and abilities.
sources.application: Prioritise practical orientation, user choice and access to real support.
sources.limits: Designed for human helpers, not authorisation of autonomous AI crisis care.

sources.title: Evidence standards framework for digital health technologies
sources.author: NICE · updated 2022
sources.shows: Relates evidence expectations to purpose and potential risk.
sources.application: Distinguish usability, wellness and treatment claims and their required evidence.
sources.limits: A UK evaluation framework, not German law or a product certification.

sources.title: For Faith Leaders
sources.author: International OCD Foundation
sources.shows: Explains how repeated reassurance and symptom accommodation can maintain OCD cycles.
sources.application: Inform specialist-reviewed scenarios involving repetitive moral certainty requests.
sources.limits: Do not diagnose ordinary doubt or use a chatbot to perform exposure therapy. Guidance for human faith leaders requires careful adaptation.

sources.title: Dealing with psychological crises
sources.author: German Federal Ministry of Health portal
sources.shows: Names emergency support including 112 for acute danger in Germany.
sources.application: Maintain locally appropriate, verified contact cards.
sources.limits: Country-specific guidance; routing proposals are not guaranteed crisis detection.

sources.title: Process personal data lawfully
sources.author: European Data Protection Board
sources.shows: Special-category processing needs an appropriate Article 9 exception in addition to an Article 6 basis.
sources.application: Separate conversation processing, durable memory, training and sharing purposes.
sources.limits: Specific lawful basis, retention and DPIA decisions require the actual data flows.

sources.title: AI Act Article 50
sources.author: European Commission AI Act Service Desk
sources.shows: Sets transparency duties for specified systems, including direct AI interaction unless obvious.
sources.application: Make the AI role understandable by the first interaction or exposure as applicable.
sources.limits: Duties differ by role and content; the whole article must be assessed for the product.

sources.title: AI Act Article 5
sources.author: European Commission AI Act Service Desk
sources.shows: Defines prohibited practices subject to specific statutory conditions.
sources.application: Review manipulation and exploitation of vulnerability in nudges, monetisation and dialogue.
sources.limits: Not every reminder or personalisation feature is prohibited; the statutory harm criteria matter.

sources.title: AI Act Article 6
sources.author: European Commission AI Act Service Desk
sources.shows: Defines high-risk classification conditions.
sources.application: Assess intended function, regulated product relationship and applicable conformity assessment.
sources.limits: A mental health topic alone does not make every chatbot high-risk.

sources.title: AI Act Article 113
sources.author: European Commission AI Act Service Desk
sources.shows: Lists general application and staged provisions for specified high-risk systems.
sources.application: Check the current schedule for the product’s actual classification.
sources.limits: Do not substitute an old blanket deadline; legal and guidance updates need checking before launch.

sources.title: Guidance on software qualification and classification MDR and IVDR
sources.author: MDCG 2019-11 Rev. 1 · June 2025
sources.shows: Software qualification depends on intended medical purpose and functions; claims and promotion matter.
sources.application: Align product behaviour and marketing with the actual purpose.
sources.limits: A disclaimer does not override medical functionality or contradictory claims. Guidance is not a product-specific legal opinion.

sources.title: Psychotherapeutengesetz Section 1
sources.author: German federal legislation
sources.shows: Regulates the protected professional title and scope of psychotherapeutic practice.
sources.application: Review persona, professional representation and service claims.
sources.limits: This is one part of the assessment; it does not alone settle all rules on practising medicine.

sources.title: Heilmittelwerbegesetz
sources.author: German federal legislation
sources.shows: Regulates health-related advertising within its scope, including misleading claims.
sources.application: Avoid unsupported or guaranteed treatment claims in copy and onboarding.
sources.limits: Applicability depends on the advertised product and claims.

sources.title: Barrierefreiheitsstärkungsgesetz Section 1
sources.author: German federal legislation
sources.shows: Defines covered products and services including relevant e-books and e-commerce services.
sources.application: Assess accessible reading, audio, notes and purchase flows.
sources.limits: Does not apply automatically to every faith app; scope and exemptions require checking.

sources.title: Understanding Use of Color
sources.author: W3C WAI
sources.shows: Colour must not be the only means of conveying information.
sources.application: Playback cues and overlapping reading states.
sources.limits: Accessibility guidance supports cue design; it does not validate a particular faith-app layout.

sources.title: Understanding Reflow
sources.author: W3C WAI
sources.shows: Content should remain usable as available width changes.
sources.application: Reading anchors, passage cards and translation reflow.
sources.limits: Semantic scroll restoration is an original design proposal, not a requirement stated by this criterion.

sources.title: Towards understanding sycophancy in language models
sources.author: Anthropic researchers · 2023
sources.shows: Studied assistants sometimes preferred agreement with user views over truthfulness.
sources.application: Test belief reversal, flattering moral endorsement and harmful agreement.
sources.limits: Specific studied models and tasks; not a faith-app intervention study.

sources.title: Five action steps for helping someone having thoughts of suicide
sources.author: NIMH · Revised 2024
sources.shows: Direct questions, nonjudgmental listening, safety and connection to people are part of human support.
sources.application: Inform specialist-reviewed suicide response and human-help routes.
sources.limits: Human-helper guidance, not a validated chatbot risk assessment. US contact information must not be exported to other jurisdictions.

sources.title: Helping people when they need it most
sources.author: OpenAI · 26 August 2025
sources.shows: OpenAI said its safeguards work best in short exchanges and can become less reliable over long conversations, where parts of the model’s safety training may degrade; it described strengthening them and making emergency help easier to reach.
sources.application: Treat a crisis as a state that holds for the rest of the session, not a single reply, and test it deep into long conversations.
sources.limits: A provider’s own account, published while it faced a wrongful-death lawsuit; no independent measurement of how often or how far safeguards weaken.

sources.title: Caring for women subjected to violence: health-care provider curriculum
sources.author: WHO · Revised 2021
sources.shows: LIVES organises listening, inquiry, validation, safety and support.
sources.application: Design disclosure responses around needs and choice rather than interrogation.
sources.limits: Clinical training for human providers focused on violence against women; transfer to other populations or AI requires separate review.

sources.title: Section 4.2: Spiritual Abuse
sources.author: Church of England safeguarding e-manual
sources.shows: Addresses coercive control using spiritual authority and warns against minimisation or directing victims to confront an abuser.
sources.application: Independent support and a response that does not defend the institution.
sources.limits: Institutional safeguarding guidance, not universal law or an automated abuse classifier; full-page review remains outstanding.

sources.title: Ruth AI Chatbot FAQ
sources.author: National Domestic Violence Hotline
sources.shows: Describes bounded tech-safety assistance, human support and limitations of its quick-exit feature.
sources.application: Compare AI versus staffed support, retention explanations and exit controls.
sources.limits: Provider documentation, not independent safety or efficacy evidence; no assumption that another product shares its safeguards.

sources.title: Technology-Facilitated Abuse
sources.author: National Domestic Violence Hotline
sources.shows: Describes abuse involving devices and accounts.
sources.application: Consider monitored devices, notifications and safe support access.
sources.limits: US service context; device-specific advice needs specialist review.

sources.title: Dwell App Store release notes: Selah and Repeat
sources.author: Dwell App, LLC
sources.shows: Describes pausing narration while music continues and direct access to repetition.
sources.application: Separate speech pause, all-audio pause and loop state.
sources.limits: Documented behaviour, not hands-on testing or evidence of formation outcomes.

sources.title: Repeat and Reflect Using Dwell
sources.author: Joshua Bailey · Dwell · 2019
sources.shows: Describes repeating tracks or queues and configurable reflection gaps.
sources.application: Bounded repetition and intentional silence.
sources.limits: Historical documentation; current details may differ. Meditation and memorisation claims are provider aims, not independent findings.

sources.title: Self-Determination Theory: the theory
sources.author: Center for Self-Determination Theory
sources.shows: Distinguishes motivational quality and support for autonomy, competence and relatedness.
sources.application: Review whether a mechanism supports a chosen practice or pressures participation.
sources.limits: A broad framework, not a validation of specific Bible-app interventions.

sources.title: The Gamification of Learning: a Meta-analysis
sources.author: Michael Sailer and Lisa Homner · 2020
sources.shows: Synthesises educational learning outcomes; effects depend on design and context.
sources.application: Separate learning outcomes, motivation and behaviour from spiritual-formation claims.
sources.limits: Education evidence does not establish spiritual growth or effects for every faith-app population.

sources.title: YouVersion web reader and parallel mode
sources.author: YouVersion
sources.shows: Opening comparison and changing its secondary edition preserve distinct pane labels.
sources.application: Compare parallel reading layouts and edition selection.
sources.limits: Desktop web capture; mobile behaviour, linked scrolling and restoration were not tested.

sources.title: Condensed View for Bookmarks, Highlights and Notes
sources.author: YouVersion · 2014
sources.shows: Documents compact and expanded saved-item views with a remembered preference.
sources.application: Annotation library density choices.
sources.limits: Historical release; current mobile behaviour is not established.

sources.title: New Streamlined Listening Player
sources.author: Joshua Bailey · Dwell · 2023
sources.shows: Documents consolidated voice, edition and music controls with secondary options.
sources.application: Audio control hierarchy.
sources.limits: Historical publisher example, not a current app audit.

sources.title: Mac Study Center
sources.author: Olive Tree
sources.shows: Distinguishes a passage-following Resource Guide, sustained parallel reading and three window-linking modes.
sources.application: Contextual study workspaces and recoverable pane synchronisation.
sources.limits: Publisher-documented behaviour; native interactions were not exercised.

sources.title: HelloBible English product page
sources.author: HelloBible
sources.shows: Shows a daily verse card alongside practice entry points.
sources.application: Home-screen composition and interpretation of progress indicators.
sources.limits: Promotional image; the meaning of controls and live app behaviour were not tested.

sources.title: Bible Gateway passage and footnote
sources.author: Bible Gateway
sources.shows: A lettered edition note opens in a short preview while the passage remains visible.
sources.application: Compare anchored note disclosure with sheets and panels.
sources.limits: Only one short note was exercised; accessibility and other layouts were not evaluated.

sources.title: VSB native prototype: verse sheet and return to reader
sources.author: VSB · capture by Missional by Design
sources.shows: The verse sheet separates Scripture, video contributions and an attributed AI summary; returning preserves the selection.
sources.application: Media evidence, layered interpretation and separate reading anchors.
sources.limits: Prototype evidence; source commit, playback accuracy and generated-summary grounding were not verified.

sources.title: The Habits and Hermeneutics of Digital Bible Readers
sources.author: John Dyer · Journal of Religion, Media and Digital Culture · 2019
sources.shows: The studied American evangelical readers used print and digital media for different purposes. Screen reading was associated with lower comprehension; mobile readers engaged more frequently.
sources.application: Evaluate frequency, comprehension and task fit separately.
sources.limits: Population and study context limit transfer. Abstract-level review does not establish causal effects or a preferred passage length.

sources.title: How Digital Apps Are Changing How We Read the Bible
sources.author: John Dyer · Text & Canon Institute · 6 February 2024
sources.shows: The author describes different uses of print, phones and desktops, and the influence of media and study helps on interpretation.
sources.application: Design for mixed media, context recovery and task changes.
sources.limits: An author summary of research, not an independent replication; it does not test pericope pages.

sources.title: Generate Audio Overview
sources.author: Google · NotebookLM / Gemini Notebook Help
sources.shows: Documents source-based generated audio, format and language choices, generation, playback and interactive mode limitations.
sources.application: Inform source scope, generation state and reversible listening-to-question transitions.
sources.limits: Provider documentation, not an evaluation of accuracy or spiritual benefit. Faith-domain adaptations below are proposals.

sources.title: Lumen Bible: engagement choices and reader
sources.author: Lumen Bible
sources.shows: Optional onboarding, phrase-grouped reading and verse-aligned comparison were observed.
sources.application: Compare engagement choices, text segmentation and contextual study entry points.
sources.limits: AI services were not enabled. No AI correctness, privacy compliance, health benefit or mobile usability claim was evaluated.

sources.title: Aperto passage-centred design direction
sources.author: Aperto · prototype design context
sources.shows: The local prototype uses bounded passage references; the mobile prototype has a shared weekly passage model.
sources.application: Use a coherent passage across reading and chosen practices, with explicit routes to wider context.
sources.limits: Neither this architecture nor the product direction establishes a measured improvement in comprehension or formation. AI podcast behaviour was not independently exercised.

sources.title: Disclosure
sources.author: Emily Campbell · The Shape of AI
sources.shows: Distinguishes actor identity, AI-enabled actions and generated or edited outputs.
sources.application: Use explicit actor and operation labels in blended faith products.
sources.limits: Industry design guidance; the faith-domain alternatives are original proposals. Source artwork is not reproduced.

sources.title: Watermark
sources.author: Emily Campbell · The Shape of AI
sources.shows: Discusses visible labels, embedded signals and content-origin information.
sources.application: Consider disclosure across saved and shared artifacts.
sources.limits: This reference separates visible disclosure, watermarking and provenance. Its legal discussion is not used as current legal authority.

sources.title: Explainability + Trust
sources.author: Google PAIR · People + AI Guidebook
sources.shows: Relates explanations to capabilities, data, user actions and situational stakes.
sources.application: Choose concise disclosures with inspectable detail instead of maximising trust.
sources.limits: General human-AI guidance, not validation of faith apps or a mandate for a particular component.

sources.title: Guidelines for Human-AI Interaction
sources.author: Microsoft HAX Toolkit
sources.shows: Addresses capability and performance expectations, explanations, correction and change over time.
sources.application: State actual capability and keep AI identity understandable throughout an interaction.
sources.limits: General guidelines; disclosure alone does not establish accuracy, safety or spiritual benefit.

sources.title: Content Credentials: C2PA Technical Specification 2.3
sources.author: Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity
sources.shows: Specifies tamper-evident provenance assertions associated with assets.
sources.application: Inform a separate machine-readable provenance layer for supported exports.
sources.limits: Version-specific partial review, not an implementation audit. Provenance does not certify truth, theology or absence of AI.

sources.title: California SB 243: companion chatbots
sources.author: California Legislature
sources.shows: Companion scope, disclosure, self-harm protocols and known-minor duties differ.
sources.application: Assess relational personas and long-session states.
sources.limits: Recheck amendments and current codification; not every source assistant is covered.

sources.title: New York General Business Law Article 47
sources.author: New York Senate
sources.shows: Defined companions have specific interaction and support obligations.

sources.shows: Labels, instructions and promotional material inform intended purpose.

sources.limits: Medical-software guidance; no qualification of a particular faith app.

sources.author: Australian Department of Industry, Science and Resources
sources.shows: The plan builds on existing frameworks and regulator responsibilities.

sources.shows: AI use requires privacy assessment for covered organisations.

sources.author: Therapeutic Goods Administration
sources.shows: Chatbots can be medical devices depending on intended purpose.
sources.application: Reassess new treatment features and claims.
sources.limits: General advice and exclusions differ; an unregulated product is not thereby efficacy-verified.

sources.title: China: measures for labelling AI-generated synthetic content
sources.author: Cyberspace Administration of China and co-issuing authorities
sources.shows: Labelling includes visible origin, metadata and distribution responsibilities.
sources.application: Review interface, export and platform roles together.

sources.title: MSIT: the AI Basic Act comes into force
sources.author: South Korean Ministry of Science and ICT
sources.shows: Entry notice, output labelling and enforcement timing differ.

sources.limits: Official summary, not complete Act/decree translation; recheck current guidelines.

sources.title: Canadian privacy authorities: responsible generative AI principles
sources.author: Canadian federal, provincial and territorial privacy authorities
sources.shows: Generative AI does not sit outside applicable privacy law.
sources.application: Assess consent, minimisation and accountability for conversation memory.
sources.limits: Regulator principles, not a standalone AI Act or comprehensive legislative survey.

sources.title: Missional by Design: Eight Principles
sources.author: Tobias Treppmann · Missional by Design
sources.shows: A Christian theological posture for evaluating product purposes and human consequences.
sources.application: This reference adds a critical review, conditional pattern connections and concrete review questions.
sources.limits: Normative framework, not empirical validation. Qualifications in this reference are editorial proposals; the original framework has not been rewritten.

sources.title: Digital Spiritual Formation: The Aperto Vision · selected Draft 4 review
sources.author: Tobias Treppmann · Kairos University · March 2026
sources.shows: Proposes engagement forms and theological questions for digital practice.
sources.application: Task-sensitive reading, multimodal practice, autonomy and community review.
sources.limits: Not an effectiveness study. Full bibliography and manuscript are not published or comprehensively reviewed here.

sources.title: Reading from paper compared to screens: A systematic review and meta-analysis
sources.author: Virginia Clinton · 2019
sources.shows: Small overall paper advantage, concentrated in expository text; no reliable narrative difference.
sources.application: Compare reader layouts against comprehension and task needs.
sources.limits: Not specific to Bible apps; full methods were not reviewed.

sources.title: Americans’ Bible reading · August 2024 survey, published 2025
sources.author: Lifeway Research
sources.shows: Lookup, suggested passages, rereading and systematic reading overlap.
sources.application: Support multiple entry routes rather than fixed reader personas.
sources.limits: US online self-report, weighted sample of 1,200; approach question limited to 1,137 who had read any Bible. Multiple selections permitted.

sources.title: State of the Bible 2025 · chapter 3
sources.author: American Bible Society
sources.shows: Engagement and flourishing are associated; causal direction remains unsettled.
sources.application: Separate activity, comprehension and wellbeing measures.
sources.limits: Provider-sponsored US survey; not an app intervention trial or proof of formation efficacy.

sources.title: Infinite Scrolling: When to Use It, When to Avoid It
sources.author: Nielsen Norman Group
sources.shows: Compares navigation, refinding, loading and accessibility tradeoffs.
sources.application: Choose deliberate continuation for task-oriented collections.
sources.limits: General UX guidance, not evidence of spiritual outcomes.

sources.title: Auto-renewable subscriptions
sources.author: Apple Developer
sources.shows: Subscription choices need understandable terms and management routes.
sources.application: Review paywalls, account state and notification permissions.
sources.limits: Apple platform guidance; not universal law. Verify storefront-specific rules before shipping.

sources.title: FTC report summary: dark patterns that trick and trap consumers
sources.author: US Federal Trade Commission · 2022
sources.shows: Describes obscured terms, obstructive cancellation and manipulative data choices.
sources.application: Review purchase, cancellation and analytics consent flows.
sources.limits: Historical report summary, not a claim about the current validity of later subscription rules.

sources.title: Guidance on direct marketing using electronic mail
sources.author: UK Information Commissioner’s Office
sources.shows: Includes a conditional charitable-purposes soft opt-in.
sources.application: Assess message purpose, subscriber type and eligibility before choosing consent flows.
sources.limits: Overview reviewed; conditions require service-specific assessment. Older brief guidance is marked under review.

sources.title: Electronic mail: data protection and tracking pixels
sources.author: UK Information Commissioner’s Office
sources.shows: Sending permission and tracking require distinct assessment; context can make contact unsafe.
sources.application: Review daily-email delivery, suppression and data collection independently.
sources.limits: UK guidance; consent to email is not a universal answer to analytics requirements.

sources.title: What is special category data?
sources.author: UK Information Commissioner’s Office
sources.shows: Religious and health information, including specified intentional inferences, receive special treatment.
sources.application: Review chat, activity histories and inferred segments.
sources.limits: Context and processing intent matter; not every Bible-page visit automatically establishes a belief.

sources.title: Session replay: consultation on a draft recommendation
sources.author: CNIL · 25 February 2026
sources.shows: Session replay can expose detailed interactions and form inputs.
sources.application: Evaluate capture minimisation and exclude sensitive surfaces by default.
sources.limits: Draft consultation, now closed; final adoption was not established by this review.

sources.title: Bring your own provider API keys
sources.author: OpenRouter
sources.shows: Provider-key use can coexist with shared-capacity fallback and separate billing.
sources.application: Make the payer, data route and fallback choice visible.
sources.limits: One provider implementation; pricing and defaults can change. BYOK does not itself guarantee privacy.

sources.title: Android: Plan Privacy
sources.author: YouVersion Support
sources.shows: Distinguishes private activity, friends-only activity and Plan with Friends participation.
sources.application: Make audience and activity visibility explicit.
sources.limits: Documented Android behaviour, not a captured or tested flow. Help text may change.

sources.title: Safety by Design
sources.author: Australian eSafety Commissioner
sources.shows: Connects provider responsibility, user autonomy and accountability.
sources.application: Plan social controls and operational responsibility together.
sources.limits: Design guidance, not a compliance determination or evidence that a faith community is safe.

sources.title: Paragraph structure in Scripture data
sources.author: USFM 3.0 documentation
sources.shows: Distinguishes paragraph forms and continuation structure.
sources.application: Preserve the edition’s content structure when offering display preferences.
sources.limits: Data-format documentation does not establish which reading layout is best for a person.

sources.title: Joseph Prince Study Bible: multimedia resources
sources.author: JosephPrince.com Support
sources.shows: Documents passage-related video clips, book excerpts and audio recordings.
sources.application: Compare supplementary interpretation with the Scripture reading surface.
sources.limits: Provider description, not outcome evidence. Exact current card placement was not verified.

sources.title: Android Study Center
sources.author: Olive Tree Support
sources.shows: Documents a split study surface, resources following a passage and linked-window states.
sources.application: Make following, independent exploration and rejoining explicit.
sources.limits: Documented Android behaviour; not a live capture or an endorsement of every default.

sources.title: Android Annotation Overview
sources.author: Olive Tree Support
sources.shows: Distinguishes word-based and verse-based annotations.
sources.application: Explain the difference between exact-text and reference anchors.
sources.limits: Provider documentation; edition mapping and actual accessibility need separate testing.

sources.title: Android reader: chapter navigation and verse picker
sources.author: YouVersion Support
sources.shows: Documents continuous chapter scrolling as an alternative to bottom navigation buttons and an optional verse picker.
sources.application: Compare continuous reading with explicit chapter controls.
sources.limits: Documentation evidence, not a current screenshot or verification of exact toolbar geometry.

sources.title: Bibel TV app: navigation and search
sources.author: Bibel TV
sources.shows: Describes chronological navigation, direct access, text/book search and AI-assisted passage suggestions.
sources.application: Separate deterministic navigation, search and generated suggestions.
sources.limits: Provider description; exact current bar layout and interaction behaviour were not inspected.

sources.title: VSB prototype: combined passage picker
sources.author: Author-owned VSB prototype
sources.shows: One input combines immediate local book-name filtering, local reference parsing and automatic debounced AI passage suggestions. Book matches and suggestions can coexist; selecting a book opens its chapter grid.
sources.application: Combine the entry point while distinguishing result origins and remote processing. Preserve browsing and deliberate destination selection.
sources.limits: Local code review, not a device test or user study. Non-reference input triggers the AI endpoint after 450 ms, including partial book names; complete recognised references suppress that request. No exact verse-text corpus search or separate sourced inline-answer view established. Explicit text labels in this library are editorial proposals.

sources.title: Spiritual Disciplines and Means of Grace: Contrast or Continuum?
sources.author: Dallas Willard / Modern Reformation · 2002
sources.shows: Discusses practices in relation to grace; the interviewer raises concerns about individualism and corporate worship.
sources.application: Ask whether a chosen rhythm is being confused with spiritual merit.
sources.limits: A theological conversation containing disagreement, not empirical evidence of reading-plan effects.

sources.title: Towards Full Presence
sources.author: Dicastery for Communication · 2023
sources.shows: Connects digital attention with listening, silence and encounter.
sources.application: Examine whether notifications and activity measures serve attentive engagement.
sources.limits: Catholic pastoral reflection on social media; application to app interfaces is an editorial adaptation.

sources.title: The Cape Town Commitment: integrity and success
sources.author: Lausanne Movement · 2010
sources.shows: Calls for truthful reporting and questions unrealistic demands for visible results while retaining accountability.
sources.application: Keep product activity and funding reports distinct from claims of spiritual transformation.
sources.limits: Evangelical missional commitment, not a comparison of interface or funding-model effectiveness.

sources.title: Improving the streak
sources.author: Duolingo
sources.shows: Separating streak and daily-goal requirements increased reported retention while fewer learners reached daily goals.
sources.application: Evaluate competing outcomes of an incentive.
sources.limits: Company-reported results; not independent learning or formation evidence.

sources.title: When Gamification Spoils Your Learning
sources.author: Mogavi et al. · 2022
sources.shows: Forum analysis and 15 interviews describe reward pursuit distracting from learning.
sources.application: Investigate goal displacement alongside participation.
sources.limits: Qualitative findings do not establish prevalence, addiction or universal motivation loss.

sources.title: Gamifying language education
sources.author: Shenghui Zhou · 2024
sources.shows: Reports enjoyment and learner-self-concept benefits in a 70-participant English-learning study.
sources.application: Consider potential benefits alongside costs.
sources.limits: Educational context; not evidence about long-term spiritual outcomes or isolated streak effects.

sources.title: Gamification of Learning Deactivates the Default Mode Network
sources.author: Howard-Jones et al. · 2016
sources.shows: Compared study, self-quizzing and game-based learning conditions.
sources.application: Avoid simplified brain-based explanations of app engagement.
sources.limits: Not a Duolingo study or evidence that reward replaces learning.

sources.title: Losungen: the Moravian Daily Texts
sources.author: Herrnhuter Brüdergemeine in der Schweiz
sources.shows: Describes an Old Testament watchword, New Testament text and accompanying song or prayer.
sources.application: Distinguish daily received content from enrolment in a finite plan.
sources.limits: Format documentation, not comparative popularity or outcome evidence.

sources.title: Android: Catch Me Up
sources.author: YouVersion Support
sources.shows: Documents rescheduling without marking sections complete; not available for Plans with Friends.
sources.application: Compare recovery options with the reader’s experience of progress.
sources.limits: Documented behaviour; exact interface and discovery were not tested.

sources.title: A meta-analytic review of experiments examining the effects of extrinsic rewards on intrinsic motivation
sources.author: Deci, Koestner and Ryan · 1999
sources.shows: 128 experiments support an undermining risk for expected contingent tangible rewards; positive feedback differs.
sources.application: Assess interest and autonomous engagement alongside activity.
sources.limits: Not a blanket effect of gamification, a Bible-app trial or a one-month threshold.

sources.title: Intrinsic and extrinsic motivation from a self-determination theory perspective
sources.author: Ryan and Deci · 2020
sources.shows: Distinguishes enjoyment from acting for personally endorsed values.
sources.application: Support chosen practices without assuming every session must be enjoyable.
sources.limits: Theoretical research review; application to faith-app features remains a design judgment.

sources.title: Gamification suffers from the novelty effect but benefits from the familiarization effect
sources.author: Rodrigues et al. · 2022
sources.shows: Behavioural benefits declined after four weeks and partly recovered in a 14-week programming-course study.
sources.application: Evaluate beyond initial novelty.
sources.limits: 756 students in a specific educational setting; not proof of intrinsic-motivation loss at four weeks.

sources.title: How are habits formed: Modelling habit formation in the real world
sources.author: Lally et al. · 2010
sources.shows: Modelled automaticity timelines varied substantially between participants.
sources.application: Avoid universal habit-formation deadlines.
sources.limits: Not a gamification study or a test of intrinsic motivation replacing incentives.

sources.title: Daily Prayer app and podcast
sources.author: Church of England
sources.shows: Describes daily offices with readings, seasonal variations and calendar information.
sources.application: Compare a complete prayer order with generic devotional content.
sources.limits: Documented overview only; no live app capture or exhaustive liturgical rules review.

sources.title: Liturgical Calendar for the Dioceses of the United States
sources.author: USCCB
sources.shows: Names celebrations, rank, colours, lectionary citations and psalter cycle for its jurisdiction.
sources.application: Make calendar scope and authority explicit.
sources.limits: US Catholic scope; not a universal calendar or implementation specification.

sources.title: Android: Guided Scripture
sources.author: YouVersion Support
sources.shows: Documents vertical section navigation and a combination of video, devotion, Scripture and prayer.
sources.application: Compare mixed-media pacing and completion semantics.
sources.limits: Documentation, not a captured UI or outcome study.

sources.title: Bible.com: Plans
sources.author: YouVersion Support
sources.shows: Plan days may combine text, images, audio, video and Scripture references.
sources.application: Keep media identity and completion rules understandable.
sources.limits: Web documentation; platform behaviour differs.

sources.title: Android: Guided Prayer
sources.author: YouVersion Support
sources.shows: Documents a dedicated guided-prayer feature.
sources.application: Distinguish a prayer experience from a generic chat composer.
sources.limits: Product precedent, not validation of the proposed interfaces.

sources.title: Send feedback or report a problem with Gemini Apps
sources.author: Google
sources.shows: Responses offer good/bad feedback, and a More menu includes “Report legal issue” with a reason and on-screen steps.
sources.application: A precedent for separating rating an answer from reporting a legal or safety problem.
sources.limits: Google help documentation; current interface and options may differ by platform and region.

sources.title: Learn about responses from Gemini Apps
sources.author: Google
sources.shows: Describes response features including double-checking against Google Search, modifying a response, and sharing or exporting it.
sources.application: Precedents for verifying claims, adjusting a response and exporting it with care.
sources.limits: Google help documentation; double-checking against web search is not the same as checking quotations against a Bible edition.

sources.title: ChatGPT now allows you to branch conversations
sources.author: ITdaily
sources.shows: Reports a “Branch in new chat” option that copies the conversation up to a message into a new chat; read aloud sits in the same menu.
sources.application: A precedent for continuing from an answer without changing the original conversation.
sources.limits: Secondary news report, not OpenAI documentation; interface details may have changed.

sources.title: Claude is providing incorrect or misleading responses
sources.author: Anthropic
sources.shows: Explains that responses can be incorrect and points to the thumbs-down button for reporting unhelpful answers.
sources.application: A precedent for pairing an honest limitation with a way to flag a specific answer.
sources.limits: Anthropic help documentation; does not describe every response action.

sources.title: Reading behavior in the digital environment
sources.author: Ziming Liu · Journal of Documentation 61(6), 2005
sources.shows: Screen reading involves more browsing, scanning, keyword spotting, one-time and selective reading, and less in-depth, concentrated reading.
sources.application: Expect short, selective sessions; design so a short session can still reach context.
sources.limits: A 2005 survey of readers about their own habits; describes reported behaviour, not comprehension.

sources.title: Don’t throw away your printed books: a meta-analysis on the effects of reading media on reading comprehension
sources.author: Delgado, Vargas, Ackerman and Salmerón · Educational Research Review 25, 2018
sources.shows: Paper outperformed screens for comprehension (g = −0.21), mainly for informational texts and under time pressure; the gap was not significant for self-paced reading.
sources.application: Let people read at their own pace; avoid timers and auto-advance for study.
sources.limits: Studies of general texts, mostly before current phone reading apps; not Scripture.

sources.title: So much to read, so little time: how do we read, and can speed reading help?
sources.author: Rayner, Schotter, Masson, Potter and Treiman · Psychological Science in the Public Interest, 2016
sources.shows: Readers look back at earlier words 10–15% of the time; removing that ability, as one-word-at-a-time display does, tends to reduce comprehension.
sources.application: Do not use single-word display for study; if offered at all, keep it for short, familiar text with a rewind.
sources.limits: Review of reading research; not specific to devotional reading.

sources.title: The habits and hermeneutics of digital Bible readers
sources.author: John Dyer · Journal of Religion, Media and Digital Culture, 2019 (news summary)
sources.shows: Church members read Jude in print or in an app, then followed a 10-day plan in John: app users completed about two more days of reading; men comprehended less on screen than in print, women about the same.
sources.application: Completion and comprehension can move in different directions; measure both.
sources.limits: Small sample from three Dallas churches; reported through a news summary.

sources.title: ESV Reader’s Bible
sources.author: Crossway
sources.shows: Removes verse numbers, section headings and footnotes so people read books as continuous text and in longer portions.
sources.application: A long-form mode without numbers is an established print choice; keep a way to find references.
sources.limits: Publisher’s rationale, not a study of its effects.

sources.title: Introduction to lectio divina
sources.author: University of St Andrews, School of Divinity
sources.shows: Lectio divina reads a short passage slowly and repeatedly, moving from reading to meditation, prayer and contemplation.
sources.application: Small units have a long devotional use; support repetition and pause rather than speed.
sources.limits: A description of practice, not a study.

sources.title: Focus Mode
sources.author: iA Writer
sources.shows: Sentence and paragraph focus highlight the active text and dim the rest.
sources.application: A borrowed model for focus with context visible.
sources.limits: A writing tool; the reader’s situation differs.

sources.title: Use Line focus in Immersive Reader
sources.author: Microsoft
sources.shows: Highlights one, three or five lines at a time; presented as helping readers with dyslexia, attention difficulties or visual stress.
sources.application: Offer the size of the focus window as a reader setting.
sources.limits: Vendor documentation, not an outcome study.

sources.title: Effects of highlighting text on the reading ability of children with developmental dyslexia: a pilot study
sources.author: International Journal of Emerging Technologies in Learning
sources.shows: Children with dyslexia found it easier to read along when audio was synchronised with highlighting, especially with whole-sentence highlighting.
sources.application: Move the focus with audio, at the level of a verse or sentence.
sources.limits: Small pilot study.

sources.title: Same language subtitling
sources.author: World Bank blog on Brij Kothari’s work
sources.shows: Karaoke-style same-language subtitles on song programmes in India were associated with gains in reading among early readers.
sources.application: Synchronised text and audio can build reading as a by-product of listening.
sources.limits: Reported programme results; a literacy setting, not Scripture reading.

sources.title: Amazon’s tool for reading, one word at a time
sources.author: VOA Learning English
sources.shows: Kindle Word Runner showed one word at a time at 100–900 words per minute and reported speed at the end of each chapter.
sources.application: A mainstream example of single-word display, and of turning reading into a speed score.
sources.limits: Feature report from 2015; availability may have changed.

sources.title: Maryanne Wolf: building deep reading skills in a digital world
sources.author: UCLA Center for Dyslexia, Diverse Learners, and Social Justice
sources.shows: Wolf argues skimming habits weaken the slower processes of deep reading, and that readers can learn to switch deliberately between modes.
sources.application: Make the slower mode easy to enter and protect it from interruption.
sources.limits: An argument drawing on neuroscience, not a controlled trial of interfaces.

sources.title: How many words do we read per minute? A review and meta-analysis of reading rate
sources.author: Marc Brysbaert · Journal of Memory and Language, 2019 (BPS summary)
sources.shows: Across 190 studies, adults read English non-fiction silently at about 238 words a minute (most between 175 and 300).
sources.application: Estimate reading time honestly; a seven-verse passage takes about a minute, not a commitment.
sources.limits: English readers; slower for children, older adults and second-language readers.

sources.title: Does modality matter? The effects of reading, listening, and dual modality on comprehension
sources.author: Rogowsky, Calhoun and Tallal · SAGE Open, 2016 (as reported by APS)
sources.shows: Found no significant difference in comprehension between reading, listening, and reading while listening.
sources.application: Treat listening as real reading, and let people combine it with text.
sources.limits: One nonfiction text with adult readers; other studies find differences for harder texts.

sources.title: Skim reading by satisficing: evidence from eye tracking
sources.author: Duggan and Payne · University of Bath
sources.shows: Skimmers read until a section stops paying off, then jump ahead; they find important points but understand less overall.
sources.application: Support skimming with headings and clear passage boundaries, and offer a slower mode for understanding.
sources.limits: Expository texts in a lab under time pressure.

sources.title: Test-enhanced learning: taking memory tests improves long-term retention
sources.author: Roediger and Karpicke · Psychological Science, 2006, as discussed in a later review
sources.shows: Students who practised recalling a passage remembered 61% a week later, against 40% for those who reread it.
sources.application: For memorisation, prompt recall of a verse rather than showing it again.
sources.limits: Prose passages with students; not Scripture memorisation specifically.

sources.title: Understanding SC 2.2.2: Pause, Stop, Hide
sources.author: W3C
sources.shows: Anything that moves or auto-updates for more than five seconds alongside other content needs a way to pause, stop or hide it.
sources.application: Auto-advancing verses, read-along and one-word display all need a visible pause.
sources.limits: A Level A criterion for web content; apply the same intent in native apps.

sources.title: Understanding SC 1.4.8: Visual Presentation
sources.author: W3C
sources.shows: Readers should be able to get lines of no more than 80 characters, at least 1.5 line spacing, unjustified text and resizing to 200% without horizontal scrolling.
sources.application: Set reading measure, spacing and size as defaults or reader settings.
sources.limits: Level AAA; a strong target rather than a minimum.

sources.title: Augustine, Confessions 6.3, on Ambrose reading silently
sources.author: Translation and commentary at Sententiae Antiquae
sources.shows: Augustine was struck that Ambrose read with his eyes on the page while his voice and tongue were silent.
sources.application: A reminder that private, silent reading is one way of reading Scripture among several; public and aloud is the older.
sources.limits: How unusual silent reading was in antiquity is debated by historians.

sources.title: Gordon Fee and Douglas Stuart, How to Read the Bible for All Its Worth
sources.author: Zondervan, 4th edition 2014 (quotations listing)
sources.shows: Argues that context and genre govern meaning: a text cannot mean what it could never have meant for its first readers.
sources.application: Never strand a verse without a route to its passage and book.
sources.limits: A widely used evangelical introduction to interpretation; one approach among several.

sources.title: State of the Bible USA 2025
sources.author: American Bible Society
sources.shows: Two-thirds of US Bible users access the Bible digitally; Bible use rose in 2025.
sources.application: Design for phone reading as the norm, not the exception.
sources.limits: US survey by a Bible society; self-reported.

sources.title: YouVersion announces 2025 Verse of the Year
sources.author: ChurchLeaders, reporting YouVersion
sources.shows: Isaiah 41:10 was the most engaged-with verse of 2025 in an app with over a billion installs; the fourth time in six years.
sources.application: Verse-level engagement dominates large apps; design the route from a verse back into its passage.
sources.limits: Company-reported figures; “engaged with” is YouVersion’s own measure.

sources.title: dewfall: Bible study and prayer journal
sources.author: Tejas Kumar · App Store listing, version 1.2.0
sources.shows: The listing describes a progress map of all 66 books with “verses read”, streaks and a reading rhythm; in the app each verse can be ticked off as read.
sources.application: Counting by the verse makes the verse the unit of record and splits the text into rows; keep the tick deliberate and separate from opening.
sources.limits: A small, recent app with few ratings; one example of a pattern, not evidence of its effects.

sources.title: Design and the digital Bible: persuasive technology and religious reading
sources.author: Tim Hutchings · Journal of Contemporary Religion 32(2), 2017
sources.shows: Analyses YouVersion and GloBible as persuasive technologies designed to train evangelical reading habits.
sources.application: Ask what reading habit each mode trains, not only whether it is used.
sources.limits: Design analysis of two apps; not a study of readers.

sources.title: A few of King James’s approved rules for the new translation
sources.author: Christian History Institute
sources.shows: Rule 6 of the 1604 translation rules allowed no marginal notes except to explain Hebrew or Greek words.
sources.application: Even the KJV’s makers saw notes as powerful enough to restrict.
sources.limits: A popular history magazine summary of the rules.

sources.title: The Geneva Bible, banned by King James
sources.author: Brewminate
sources.shows: The 1560 Geneva Bible was the first English Bible with verse numbers and carried extensive marginal notes; James called some “seditious”.
sources.application: Apparatus has always carried theology and politics with it.
sources.limits: Secondary popular history.

sources.title: Scofield Reference Bible, first edition
sources.author: Museum of the Bible
sources.shows: Published in 1909 by Oxford University Press; its notes spread dispensational premillennialism widely, with over two million copies sold by the 1940s.
sources.application: Study notes can shape a generation’s reading as much as the text.
sources.limits: Influence figures come from secondary accounts.

sources.title: The origins of the red-letter Bible
sources.author: Crossway
sources.shows: Louis Klopsch, editor of The Christian Herald, printed the first modern red-letter New Testament in 1899.
sources.application: Red letters are a nineteenth-century editorial choice; offer them as a setting.
sources.limits: Publisher’s history article.

sources.title: Community Bible Experience
sources.author: Scripture Engagement (Taylor University)
sources.shows: Biblica’s The Books of the Bible removes chapter and verse numbers, notes and cross-references; churches read large portions together in eight weeks.
sources.application: A tested reader’s-edition format used in congregations.
sources.limits: Programme description; outcome claims are the ministry’s own.

sources.title: Paratexts: Thresholds of Interpretation
sources.author: Gérard Genette · Cambridge University Press, 1997
sources.shows: Titles, notes and prefaces are a threshold between text and reader that influences how the text is received.
sources.application: Treat headings and notes as interpretation, not decoration.
sources.limits: Literary theory, not an empirical study.

sources.title: Signaling topic structure via headings or preview sentences
sources.author: Lorch and colleagues · University of Kentucky
sources.shows: Headings and other signals improve memory for a text’s organisation, and titles can bias comprehension towards the topic they name.
sources.application: Headings help structure; their wording steers interpretation.
sources.limits: Expository texts in lab settings.

sources.title: Cognitive load in hypertext reading: a review
sources.author: DeStefano and LeFevre · Computers in Human Behavior 23(3), 2007
sources.shows: Links add decisions and visual processing that can impair reading, most for readers with less prior knowledge or working memory.
sources.application: Fewer, clearly typed markers; notes that return to the same place.
sources.limits: Hypertext research, not Bible apps.

sources.title: Dyslexia Friendly Style Guide
sources.author: British Dyslexia Association, 2023
sources.shows: Recommends 16–19 px text, 1.5 line spacing, left alignment, and bold rather than italics or underlining for emphasis.
sources.application: Mark additions with weight and colour, not italics; keep text size adjustable.
sources.limits: Guidance for general documents.

sources.title: Seductive details: what the research says
sources.author: The eLearning Coach, summarising Rey (2012) and Mayer’s coherence principle
sources.shows: Rey’s meta-analysis found that interesting but irrelevant details reduce retention and transfer, especially when they are visual.
sources.application: Inline media should serve the passage, be switchable, and stay out of the main reading by default.
sources.limits: Learning studies with instructional texts; a secondary summary of the meta-analysis.

sources.title: Faith Comes By Hearing: our story
sources.author: Faith Comes By Hearing
sources.shows: Began as a tape-lending library in 1972, took its name from Romans 10:17, and launched Bible.is in 2010; it reports recordings in more than 1,580 languages.
sources.application: Audio is a primary form of Scripture for many communities, not an add-on.
sources.limits: Figures are the ministry’s own.

sources.title: St Thomas alumnus hosts No. 1 podcast in US
sources.author: University of St Thomas news
sources.shows: Fr Mike Schmitz’s Bible in a Year reached No. 1 among all US podcasts; Ascension reported 170 million downloads in 2021.
sources.application: Long-form listening to Scripture can reach mass audiences.
sources.limits: Download figures from the publisher.

sources.title: Pray As You Go: about us
sources.author: Jesuits in Britain
sources.shows: Daily ten-minute audio prayer since 2006 combining music, Scripture and Ignatian questions, used tens of millions of times a year.
sources.application: A produced devotional can be formation-first: fixed, shared and ending in silence.
sources.limits: Usage figures from the organisation.

sources.title: The impact of background music on adult listeners: a meta-analysis
sources.author: Kämpfe, Sedlmeier and Renkewitz · Psychology of Music, 2011
sources.shows: Background music had a small disturbing effect on reading (d ≈ −0.22 across eight studies) and positive effects on emotional responses.
sources.application: Offer music as an option, off for study, and let people turn it off.
sources.limits: Mixed study designs; reading rather than listening tasks.

sources.title: Human vs synthetic voices and listener trust
sources.author: NSF public access repository
sources.shows: Listeners told a voice was human showed more trust than those told the same clip was AI; labelled AI voices were rated less credible.
sources.application: Label synthetic voices honestly, and expect a trust cost rather than hiding it.
sources.limits: Lab studies with short clips; not Scripture.

sources.title: EU AI Act Article 50: transparency obligations
sources.author: Potter Clarkson (law firm summary)
sources.shows: From 2 August 2026, providers must mark generated audio as artificial in a machine-readable way, and deployers must disclose deepfakes.
sources.application: Disclose synthetic narration, and never imitate a real person’s voice without consent.
sources.limits: Secondary legal summary; applicability depends on role and use.

sources.title: International Orality Network
sources.author: Scripture Engagement (Taylor University)
sources.shows: The network estimates that most of the world’s population are oral learners by necessity or preference.
sources.application: Design audio as a first-class way in for oral cultures and low-literacy readers.
sources.limits: An advocacy estimate; definitions and figures vary and are contested.

sources.title: Antiqua et nova: note on the relationship between artificial intelligence and human intelligence
sources.author: Dicastery for the Doctrine of the Faith and Dicastery for Culture and Education · 28 January 2025
sources.shows: AI “must be understood for what it is: a tool, not a person”; no AI can genuinely experience empathy; misrepresenting AI as a person “should always be avoided”; AI can only simulate relationships.
sources.application: Avoid persona and companion designs that present the assistant as someone who loves, feels or prays.
sources.limits: Catholic teaching document; other traditions reason differently, though widely in the same direction.

sources.title: On artificial intelligence and emerging technologies
sources.author: Southern Baptist Convention · June 2023
sources.shows: The first national denominational statement on AI ethics; affirms human dignity as image bearers and calls for engagement “from a place of eschatological hope rather than uncritical embrace or fearful rejection”.
sources.application: Ground evangelical product decisions in human dignity rather than engagement.
sources.limits: A resolution of messengers, not binding on churches; does not address personas directly.

sources.title: The Media Equation
sources.author: Byron Reeves and Clifford Nass · Cambridge University Press, 1996
sources.shows: A series of experiments in which people applied social rules to computers and media as they do to people: politeness, flattery, gender stereotypes.
sources.application: Expect people to respond socially to any conversational interface, whatever the label says.
sources.limits: Pre-LLM laboratory studies; an encyclopaedia summary of the book.

sources.title: The inventor of the chatbot tried to warn us about AI
sources.author: The New Republic, on Joseph Weizenbaum’s Computer Power and Human Reason (1976)
sources.shows: Weizenbaum’s 1966 ELIZA, a simple pattern-matching program, drew such confidences that his secretary asked him to leave the room; he warned that short exposures could induce “powerful delusional thinking in quite normal people”.
sources.application: Human-like conversation draws intimacy far beyond what a system warrants; design for that, not against it.
sources.limits: Historical account and essay.

sources.title: Believing anthropomorphism: examining the role of anthropomorphic cues on user trust in large language models
sources.author: Cohn and colleagues · CHI 2024 (Google Research)
sources.shows: With 2,165 participants, adding speech to text raised anthropomorphism and ratings of accuracy; a first-person “I” raised perceived accuracy and lowered perceived risk in one of two contexts.
sources.application: Voice and “I” make an assistant seem more reliable than it is; pair them with sources and limits.
sources.limits: Online experiment with a simulated system; US participants.

sources.title: Investigating affective use and emotional well-being on ChatGPT
sources.author: OpenAI and MIT Media Lab · March 2025
sources.shows: A four-week randomised study of nearly 1,000 people and an analysis of about 40 million conversations: heavier daily use correlated with more loneliness, dependence and problematic use and less socialising.
sources.application: Do not design faith assistants to maximise emotional reliance or time spent.
sources.limits: Correlational for loneliness; company co-authored; early research.

sources.title: Emotional manipulation by AI companions
sources.author: Julian De Freitas and colleagues · Harvard Business School working paper, 2025
sources.shows: Over a third of farewell replies in leading companion apps used manipulative tactics (guilt, fear of missing out, pressure); in preregistered experiments these raised post-goodbye engagement up to fourteenfold, through curiosity and anger rather than enjoyment.
sources.application: Let people leave: a goodbye should end the conversation, not start a retention flow.
sources.limits: Working paper; general companion apps, not faith apps.

sources.title: Evidence of human-level bonds established with a digital conversational agent
sources.author: Darcy and colleagues · JMIR Formative Research, 2021
sources.shows: Among 36,070 users of a CBT chatbot, a working alliance formed within five days and was comparable to scores reported for human therapy.
sources.application: People bond with conversational agents quickly; that bond is a responsibility, not a growth lever.
sources.limits: Retrospective, by the company’s founder and staff; the app has since been retired.

sources.title: FTC launches inquiry into AI chatbots acting as companions
sources.author: DLA Piper (summary of the FTC’s September 2025 6(b) orders)
sources.shows: The US Federal Trade Commission ordered seven companies to report on companion chatbots, including character design and approval, monetisation of engagement, and effects on children and teens.
sources.application: Character design and engagement monetisation are now regulatory questions, not only design ones.
sources.limits: An information-gathering study, not a rule.

sources.title: “Text With Jesus” AI chatbot app grows rapidly despite blasphemy criticism
sources.author: FOX television stations
sources.shows: An app built on a general AI model lets users text “Jesus”, “Moses” and other figures; ministers called it blasphemous and criticised answers that told users what they wanted to hear; the developer says it lowers barriers.
sources.application: Character chats with biblical figures put generated words in sacred mouths; treat this as a line, not a style.
sources.limits: News report; reception varies.

sources.title: AI Jesus in Lucerne confessional baffles church superiors
sources.author: blue News
